plan.title: Framework upgrade reverts Dependabot's actions/checkout bump on deposited deft-core-guard.yml (churn loop)

narratives.Description: Framework upgrade reverts Dependabot's actions/checkout bump on deposited deft-core-guard.yml (churn loop). This story closes the linked GitHub issue with a scoped fix, tests, and a CHANGELOG entry. File scope and verify commands are recorded under plan.metadata.swarm for concurrent allocation.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Every framework upgrade silently **reverts a merged Dependabot bump** on the deposited `deft-core-guard.yml` workflow, because two directive-owned mechanisms fight each other:

1. `cmd/deft-install/deposit.go` hardcodes `actions/checkout@v4` and **overwrites** the consumer's `deft-core-guard.yml` wholesale on every upgrade.
2. The deposited `dependabot.yml` enables the `github-actions` ecosystem, so Dependabot scans the consumer's `.github/workflows/**` — including the deposited guard — and bumps `actions/checkout`.

Result: an infinite ping-pong. Dependabot bumps `@v4 → @v6`; the next `deft-install --upgrade` reverts it to `@v4`; next week Dependabot bumps it again; the next upgrade reverts it again.

## Evidence (observed on a real consumer: deftai/cartograph)

`git log` for `.github/workflows/deft-core-guard.yml` in cartograph:

```
3c0a161 chore(deft): update framework payload to v0.50.0 (#56)   <- reverted @v6 -> @v4
61092d5 chore(deps): bump actions/checkout from 4 to 6 (#41)     <- dependabot[bot], merged
c4185d5 chore(deft): update framework payload (#39)
```

- #41 was authored by `dependabot[bot]` (`chore(deps): bump actions/checkout from 4 to 6`) and merged.
- #56 (the v0.50.0 upgrade) overwrote the file and reset it to `@v4`. Greptile flagged the apparent "downgrade" on that PR, which is what surfaced this.

In the directive source, `cmd/deft-install/deposit.go:212` has shipped `actions/checkout@v4` since the file was first created (`d7c6c14`, #1429/#1430) — it was never `@v6` upstream, confirming the `@v6` originated from the consumer-side Dependabot bump, not a directive change.

## Why it's a bug (not just cosmetic)

- **Reverts a legitimate, merged supply-chain update.** The deposited guard is permanently pinned to a stale `actions/checkout@v4` that can never stay bumped in any consumer.
- **Recurs forever.** Directive actively fights its own deposited Dependabot config on every upgrade.
- **Inconsistent with directive's own policy.** Directive's own workflows pin checkout to a SHA per #1072:
  ```
  .github/workflows/ci.yml:36:      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6.0.3
  .github/workflows/release.yml:40: - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6.0.3
  ```
  i.e. directive itself runs v6.0.3 (SHA-pinned), but deposits a stale plain `@v4` tag to consumers — a weaker and staler standard than it holds itself to, and a direct contradiction of the #1072 SHA-pinning hardening.

## Proposed fix (combination recommended)

1. **Refresh + SHA-pin the deposited action** in `deposit.go` to match directive's own #1072 policy: `actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6.0.3` instead of the plain `@v4` tag.
2. **Stop the churn structurally** — the deposited `deft-core-guard.yml` is a machine-managed file with a single owner (the installer), so it should not also be a Dependabot target. Add a Dependabot `ignore` for the guard workflow's actions in the deposited `dependabot.yml` (e.g. ignore `actions/checkout` for the guard, or scope the `github-actions` ecosystem to exclude installer-managed workflows). Otherwise even a SHA-pin will keep getting bumped by Dependabot and reverted by the next upgrade.
3. (Optional) Have `deft-install` detect when the only delta on the deposited guard is a consumer/Dependabot action-version bump and treat the consumer copy as authoritative rather than blindly overwriting — but (1)+(2) resolve the loop more simply.

## Cross-reference

Surfaced during the v0.49.0 -> v0.50.0 consumer upgrade on deftai/cartograph (PR #56). Related installer-UX guidance gap filed separately as #1671.

## Issue comment thread

_The issue body is the original write-up; maintainer comments below may supersede it. Read the full thread before building a dispatch envelope (#2143)._

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-07-10T00:37:19Z)

## Recommended disposition (2026-07-09)

**Keep open — retarget to the TypeScript deposit path. Do not fix in Go.**

The original write-up blames `cmd/deft-install/deposit.go` hardcoding `actions/checkout@v4`. That Go path is frozen (#1912). The **live** churn loop still exists on npm:

- `packages/core/src/init-deposit/scaffold.ts` → `coreGuardWorkflowContent()` still embeds `actions/checkout@v4` and refreshes `.github/workflows/deft-core-guard.yml` on init/update (vendored / tracked `.deft/core` layouts per #2148).
- Consumer Dependabot (github-actions ecosystem) can still bump that deposited workflow; the next `directive update` can still overwrite it back to `@v4`.

So #1672 is **not moot** — only the implementation surface moved from Go → TS.

### Suggested fix options (pick one primary; combine if needed)

1. **Stop overwriting consumer action pins (preferred minimal)**  
   On refresh, if `deft-core-guard.yml` already exists and only the `actions/checkout@…` pin differs, **preserve** the consumer’s pin (or any non-allowlist drift that is not the guard script body). Refresh allowlist / run-script content without clobbering the `uses:` line.

2. **Pin by commit SHA in the deposited template**  
   Deposit `actions/checkout@<full-sha>` (with a comment naming the tag) instead of a moving major tag. Dependabot still may open bumps, but the intent is “framework-owned pin,” and SHA pins are the usual hardening pattern. Pair with docs that Dependabot PRs on this file are expected to be closed or absorbed only via framework upgrade.

3. **Exclude the guard workflow from Dependabot**  
   If we deposit / maintain `.github/dependabot.yml`, add an `ignore` (or path exclude) for `.github/workflows/deft-core-guard.yml` / `actions/checkout` on that file so Dependabot stops opening the ping-pong PRs. Only works where Dependabot config is under our control.

4. **Stop depositing `deft-core-guard.yml` on npm-gitignored layouts (already partially done)**  
   #2148 already skips the guard when `.deft/core` is not tracked. Confirm cartograph-class **vendored** consumers are the only remaining churn class; document that gitignored npm deposits should not see this loop.

5. **Make the guard template a “managed block” with a stable exterior**  
   Wrap only the allowlist / script in managed markers; leave `uses: actions/checkout@…` outside the managed region so upgrades never rewrite the pin.

### Acceptance sketch

- [ ] Repro on a fixture: Dependabot-style bump of checkout in `deft-core-guard.yml`, then `directive update` — pin is **not** silently reverted (or Dependabot never proposes the bump).
- [ ] Tests under `packages/core/src/init-deposit/` cover refresh preservation / SHA pin / dependabot ignore (whichever option lands).
- [ ] CHANGELOG notes the consumer-visible end of the upgrade↔Dependabot ping-pong.
- [ ] Go `cmd/deft-install/deposit.go` left unchanged (frozen bridge).

Refs #1912, #2148, #1478, `packages/core/src/init-deposit/scaffold.ts` (`coreGuardWorkflowContent`).

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-07-10T00:47:58Z)

## Locked decision (2026-07-09)

**Ship options 1 + 2 together** — that pair is the accepted fix for this issue. Other options from the prior comment are optional extras, not required to close.

### In scope (Closes #1672)

1. **Preserve consumer `actions/checkout@…` pin on refresh**  
   When `directive update` / init-deposit refreshes `.github/workflows/deft-core-guard.yml`, do not clobber an existing consumer pin if only the `uses:` line differs. Refresh allowlist / guard script body without reverting Dependabot (or manual) bumps.

2. **Pin by commit SHA in the deposited template**  
   New deposits of `coreGuardWorkflowContent()` use `actions/checkout@<full-sha>` (with a comment naming the tag), not a floating `@v4` major tag. Lives in `packages/core/src/init-deposit/scaffold.ts` (TS path only).

### Out of scope for this issue

- Go `cmd/deft-install/deposit.go` — frozen bridge (#1912); leave unchanged.
- Options 3–5 (Dependabot ignore, docs-only #2148 clarification, managed-block exterior) — nice-to-haves; **not** required to close once 1+2 land with tests + CHANGELOG.

### Acceptance (updated)

- [ ] Fixture: existing guard with bumped checkout pin → `directive update` preserves the pin while refreshing managed guard content.
- [ ] New deposit template uses a commit-SHA pin for `actions/checkout` (documented tag in a comment).
- [ ] Tests under `packages/core/src/init-deposit/`.
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` — Closes #1672.
narratives.UserStory: As a consumer with Dependabot, I want directive update to preserve my actions/checkout pin on deft-core-guard.yml, so that framework upgrades stop reverting Dependabot bumps.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. In packages/core/src/init-deposit/scaffold.ts coreGuardWorkflowContent(), deposit actions/checkout@FULL_SHA with a comment naming the tag (option 2). 2. On refresh of existing deft-core-guard.yml, preserve an existing uses: actions/checkout@… pin when refreshing allowlist/script body (option 1). 3. Add packages/core/src/init-deposit tests for preserve-on-refresh and SHA template. 4. Verify with pnpm -C packages/core exec vitest run src/init-deposit; CHANGELOG Closes #1672. Do not edit cmd/deft-install.
